title: Perfect coherent derived direct image for proper flat algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a flat proper finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Flatness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation, flat over $T$: on each etale scheme chart it is an associated module sheaf, locally has a presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to\mathcal F\to0$ with $m,n$ finite, and its stalks are flat over the corresponding stalks of $T$. Write $f_{\mathrm{et}}:X_{\mathrm{et}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the induced morphism of small etale ringed topoi, and $\epsilon_T:T_{\mathrm{et}}\to T_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ for restriction to the Zariski site. Derived categories of modules on these sites are localizations of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set
$$K_f(\mathcal F)=R\epsilon_{T,*}Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal F\in D(\mathcal O_T)$$
[def-pc-derived-category]. Then $K_f(\mathcal F)$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. The pullback $\epsilon_T^*$ on module sheaves is exact, and the canonical counit is an isomorphism in the derived category of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$,
$$\epsilon_T^*K_f(\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal F.$$
For every morphism of schemes $h:T'\to T$, write $X'=X\times_TT'$, $f':X'\to T'$ and $\mathcal F'$ for the ordinary module pullback of $\mathcal F$. The canonical derived base-change morphism is an isomorphism
$$Lh^*K_f(\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{f'}(\mathcal F')$$
in $D(\mathcal O_{T'})$, with derived pullback as in [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Under the displayed etale--Zariski counit isomorphisms this is the usual derived base-change morphism on the small etale sites. These canonical isomorphisms respect identities and composition of base changes. For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, they take the derived scalar unit $\mathcal O_T[0]\to K_f(\mathcal O_X)$ to the scalar unit for $f'$. No fibre-dimension bound, reducedness or Noetherianness of $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CTM (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), with Tag 071Q (lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site), Tag 08H8 (lemma-epsilon-flat), Tag 08HG (lemma-descend-perfect), and Tag 08GH (remark-match-total-direct-images) for the Zariski convention.

proof.text: Put $A=Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal F$. In [lem-sfb-proper-support-tensor-perfect] take $S=Y=T$, $E=\mathcal O_X[0]$ and $G^\bullet=\mathcal F[0]$. The first factor is strictly perfect of rank one; tensoring it with $G^\bullet$ is canonically $\mathcal F[0]$. The sole term has the assumed finite presentation and relative flatness, and its support is closed in the proper space $X$, hence proper over $T$: a closed subspace is separated, finite type, and remains closed after every base change, and restricting a proper map to it preserves all three properties. Thus $A$ is etale-perfect. It has quasi-coherent cohomology by the same cited statement.

source.place: 0CTM (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), specialization of 0A1P with a single term; 08JL (lemma-pseudo-coherent), strict-perfect chart argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] to $A$. Its quasi-inverse gives $K=R\epsilon_{T,*}A\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ and its canonical counit gives $\epsilon_T^*K\simeq A$. It also gives exactness of $\epsilon_T^*$. By [lem-sfb-etale-detects-perfect], $K$ is Zariski-perfect, because its etale pullback is the perfect object $A$ from Step 1.

Let $h:T'\to T$, $q:X'\to X$, and $A'=Rf'_{\mathrm{et},*}(q^*\mathcal F)$. Properness makes $f$ quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-complex-base-change] to $E=\mathcal O_X[0]$ and $G^\bullet=\mathcal F[0]$. Its canonical map becomes an isomorphism $b_h:Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*A\to A'$, since $Lq^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X'}$ and the second factor is explicitly the ordinary $q^*\mathcal F$. In particular $A'$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Indeed $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ by Step 2, so by [lem-pc-derived-pullback-qcoh-component] every $H^n(Lh^*K)$ is quasi-coherent on each affine open $U\subseteq T'$ with $h(U)$ inside an affine open of $T$; these $U$ cover $T'$ and quasi-coherence is local, so $Lh^*K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{T'})$. The pullback comparison of [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] identifies $Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*A\simeq Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*\epsilon_T^*K$ with $\epsilon_{T'}^*Lh^*K$, which lies in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{T',\mathrm{et}})$ by the equivalence, and $b_h$ is an isomorphism onto $A'$. Thus the counit comparison also applies to $A'$. No inference that $Lq^*\mathcal F=q^*\mathcal F$ from relative flatness is used.

source.place: 0A1K (lemma-base-change-tensor), exact target and coefficient comparison in its proof; 08GH (remark-match-total-direct-images).

proof.text:
The image under $\epsilon_{T'}^*$ of the required map is the composite
$$\epsilon_{T'}^*Lh^*K\simeq Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*\epsilon_T^*K\longrightarrow Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*A\xrightarrow{b_h}A'\simeq\epsilon_{T'}^*R\epsilon_{T',*}A'.$$
All arrows are isomorphisms by Steps 2--3 and [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence]. Full faithfulness therefore gives its unique Zariski isomorphism $Lh^*K\to K_{f'}(\mathcal F')$. It is the canonical base-change map. The canonical map for the composite morphisms $\epsilon_T\circ f_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\epsilon_{T'}\circ f'_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the exchange for the composite adjunction $Lf_{\mathrm{et}}^*\epsilon_T^*\dashv R\epsilon_{T,*}Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}$ followed by $R\epsilon_{T',*}$ of the coefficient map. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) that exchange is $R\epsilon_{T',*}$ of the $f$-exchange composed with the $\epsilon$-exchange $Lh^*R\epsilon_{T,*}A\to R\epsilon_{T',*}Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*A$, the mate of the pullback comparison. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] the transpose of the latter under $\epsilon_{T'}^*\dashv R\epsilon_{T',*}$ is $\epsilon_{T'}^*Lh^*K\simeq Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*\epsilon_T^*K\to Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*A$, the pullback comparison followed by the counit. Hence the transpose of the canonical Zariski map is the displayed composite without its last arrow, and since the counit at $A'$ is invertible, its image under $\epsilon_{T'}^*$ is the displayed composite. This also proves the asserted identification with the small-etale derived base-change map.

source.place: 071Q and 08GH: transport the precise canonical 0A1K morphism through the equivalence.

proof.text: For $T''\xrightarrow{k}T'\xrightarrow{h}T$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1) to the two derived pullback squares defining exchange; their paste is the square for $hk$. The coefficient comparisons paste too: after a K-flat resolution, the maps to ordinary pullbacks send a tensor $c\otimes b\otimes m$ to $cb\otimes m$ in either order. Hence $b_{hk}=b_k\circ Lk_{\mathrm{et}}^*b_h$ after the canonical pullback comparisons. The identity case is [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](4), and the coefficient map is then the identity. The identity and composition compatibility of the site comparisons in [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] transfers both equalities to the displayed Zariski isomorphisms; faithfulness ensures equality of those actual morphisms.

source.place: 0A1K; sites-cohomology.tex 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal), verification by the existing mate-pasting theorem.

proof.text: For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, write $u_f:\mathcal O_T\to A$ for the derived adjunction unit at the structure module. The transpose of $b_h\circ Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*u_f$ is $Lq^*(\varepsilon_f\circ Lf^*u_f)$, after identifying pullbacks of structure modules with structure modules. The triangle identity makes this the identity of $\mathcal O_{X'}$. The transpose of $u_{f'}$ is also that identity, so the adjunction bijection gives $b_h\circ Lh_{\mathrm{et}}^*u_f=u_{f'}$. Here the ordinary coefficient comparison for the structure module is its scalar multiplication identification. This uses the mate definition in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The scalar-insertion normalization and canonical unit/counit of [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] give the same equality for $\mathcal O_T[0]\to K$. Thus the Zariski base-change isomorphism preserves the scalar unit.

source.place: 0A1K canonical mate definition; 071Q and 08GH equivalence normalization; triangle-identity calculation for the scalar unit.
